prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System advises; never autonomously dispatches. Aliases: Duty Detection Officer=Orion; Air Attack Supervisor=Redtail; Caldera Incident Command Portal=Emberhall; Horizon Ridge Drone Dock=Kestrel; Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine=Lantern; MesoWest Weather Fusion Node=Brindle; Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console=Marigold; VHF Radio Gateway Repeater=Badger. Smoke Classifier Module sends Orion confidence/growth/obscuration/Ridge Shadow Mask/warnings; degraded detections advisory, never commitment justification. North Lookout Camera Mast supplies Thermal Spot Snippet/bearings; South Lookout Camera Mast supplies bearings/Camera Cleaning Log; both report health. Brindle publishes Wind Shift Bulletin/exposure/recomputations; caches weather. Lantern fuses perimeter/growth/weather/fuels/reconnaissance; confidence/time-validity required. Imagery requires orthorectification/grid-registration; configuration signed/versioned; retain approved configuration offline. Redtail approves reconnaissance/drops/intent/conflicts. Delayed Confirmed Ignition State blocks dispatch; changes require assignment-review. Airspace Restricted State requires route/altitude acceptance and Helitack Crew Leader boundary-confirmation. Drone Tasking Service tracks/packages missions, avoids aviation-lanes; validates County Emergency Liaison’s Drone Corridor Permit before degraded-communications release; no independent authority. Kestrel reports readiness/health/recovery; maintenance controller produces Battery Swap Ticket; Drone Pilot Operator confirms safety/readiness. Marigold validates Runway Release Note/Suppression Drop Receipt; blocks unapproved/unready releases. East Retardant Loading Pump supplies Retardant Batch Slip; pressure-variance triggers recirculation. Tanker Base Manager verifies assignment/quantity, coordinates West Retardant Loading Pump; shift-inspection precedes availability. Emberhall audits provenance/uncertainty/Crew Staging Pin/assignments/acknowledgments. Disconnected: timestamp caches, queue authorized updates, prohibit irreversible releases. Crewline Mobile Tablet rejects expired packages; encrypted queues preserve author/device/server times. Access: least-privilege named accounts/MFA or expiring signed credentials plus restoration-review. Retention: agency incident-period; raw sensors approved shorter schedule; encryption-at-rest, controlled exports, authorized documented deletion. Multi-period resilience: stage power/network/cleaning/recovery supplies/procedures against single faults. Training: preseason/change-refreshed, role-based; Orion

New part:
S211: All operational users shall receive communications training that includes VHF Radio Gateway Repeater failure modes, alternate contact paths, call signs, message brevity, and confirmation readbacks.
S212: Weather training shall explain how the MesoWest Weather Fusion Node supports situational awareness and how operators should treat weather inputs when local observations conflict with displayed values.
S213: Initial qualification shall include supervised console practice, scenario walkthroughs, and a documented check by an instructor who is authorized by the operations lead.
S214: Annual refresher training shall include changes to software screens, revised thresholds, updated contact rosters, seasonal hazard briefings, and lessons learned from prior incidents.
S215: Tabletop exercises shall be conducted before the expected peak fire period and shall test detection triage, command notification, airspace coordination, tanker-base coordination, crew deployment, and public-agency liaison actions.
S216: Live exercises shall be scheduled at least once per season when conditions permit and shall include field crews, aircraft coordination staff, drone operations staff, and command-center personnel.
S217: Exercise controllers shall inject realistic complications such as intermittent network service, obscured camera views, delayed field confirmation, resource conflicts, and conflicting reports from external observers.
S218: Performance measures shall include time from automated detection to human review, time from review to command notification, time to resource assignment, communication completion rate, and accuracy of incident status updates.
S219: Detection quality shall be evaluated using confirmed events, benign smoke sources, weather-related artifacts, and operator notes so that both missed detections and false alarms are visible to program management.
S220: Every false-alarm review shall identify the apparent cause, affected sensors or analytic outputs, operator actions, dispatch consequences, and any recommended tuning or training change.
S221: The review board shall include operations, aviation, field crew, maintenance, and county liaison representatives when the event affected more than one operational function.
S222: Seasonal readiness shall require each active user to demonstrate current proficiency, complete required safety briefings, and acknowledge the current operating procedures before receiving operational access.
S223: Personnel who do not meet proficiency requirements shall complete remedial training and a repeat evaluation before performing unsupervised duties in the Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System.
S224: Deployment governance for the Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System shall be managed as a staged release process that follows completion of seasonal readiness activities.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
